quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can get in the way of the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They improve your grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Wearing gloves while riding improves your grip and protects your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of tough material.

questions.question: What are the best colors for motorcycle riders to wear?
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, and green are the best colors to wear. Other drivers can see these colors more easily.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get over the surface faster.
Zigzag to get the attention of other drivers.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the grooves or gratings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the grooves or gratings.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on grooves or gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Do not try to fight the weave by zigzagging, as this is more dangerous.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually safest?
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. A good rider changes position based on road and traffic conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center lane position is usually safest.

questions.question: To make it easier for other motorists to see you, you should:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you, day or night.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.explanation: Choose sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, move to another lane and give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your lane position:

options.text: Has little effect on whether other drivers can see you.
Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It can also protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: Wind noise while riding:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.

questions.explanation: Long exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Use ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for a motorcycle operator?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles give the best protection. Laced-up boots are best. If you wear shoes with long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, restaurants, and hospitals.

questions.question: How do reflective and brightly-colored helmets and clothing help motorcycle riders?

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Can help motorcycle riders be more visible.
Do not increase a motorcycle rider's safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help motorcycle riders be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you on the road.

questions.question: How should a helmet fit to give the most protection?
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long motorcycle trip?
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks to rest, even if you are not tired. Experienced riders do not ride more than six hours per day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tired faster, so dress to protect yourself from the weather.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Should only be used in an emergency.
Should be used with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When should riders use their headlights?
questions.explanation: Use your headlight all the time. Other drivers see your headlight before they notice your motorcycle. South Carolina law requires your headlight to be on whenever you are riding.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers the traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What should you check before every motorcycle ride?

options.text: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
Make sure the paint on the bike is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test each brake to make sure it activates the brake lights.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road show?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden speed or direction changes can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake smoothly.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before riding. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Bright-colored clothing so others can see you.
Any color because drivers can easily see you in daylight.
Dark-colored clothing to stand out against the bright sun.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothing so others can see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright-colored clothing at all times to make yourself more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes when braking.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: The effects are less dangerous than using either alone.
The effects balance each other out.
The effects can be stronger than using either alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects can be stronger than using either alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can impair your riding ability. Some drugs become more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights are flashing at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before proceeding. Never try to cross ahead of a train.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black text or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: What is required about motorcycle footrests?

options.text: The driver and passenger can share them.
Both the driver and passenger need their own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the driver and passenger need their own.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for both the driver and passenger. Proper footing keeps your passenger from falling and taking you with them.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loose so it flaps in the wind.

questions.explanation: Riding clothing should protect you while keeping you comfortable. Your jacket and pants should fit snugly enough to not flap in the wind, but loose enough to move freely.
